claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy has a continuous, coarse dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The lamellar microstructure typically consists of BCC/B2 and FCC phases.
The initial alloy has high strength but low room-temperature tensile ductility because of brittle interfacial cracking.
Severe plastic deformation followed by a short, low-temperature anneal will transform continuous eutectic lamellae into discontinuous equiaxed or elongated globular phase patterns.
A true strain greater than 4 is sufficient to initiate the proposed lamellar disruption.
Deformation at 300–500°C and a strain rate of 10^-2 to 10^-1 s^-1 will balance work hardening and dynamic recovery during SPD.
Annealing at 400–600°C, described as 0.4–0.5 Tm, for 10–30 minutes will cause partial spheroidization without full coarsening.
SPD produces a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations at phase interfaces.
Interfacial dislocation accumulation increases interfacial energy and drives morphological instability of the lamellae.
The post-deformation anneal enables curvature-driven interface migration, spheroidization, and dislocation annihilation.
Fragmenting the continuous phases eliminates long-range stress concentrators and interrupts brittle interfacial crack paths.
The patterned microstructure will promote uniform plasticity through grain-boundary sliding and dislocation cross-slip.
The patterned microstructure will delocalize strain and suppress crack nucleation at phase interfaces.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation by more than 50% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will reduce yield strength by less than 15% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will shift failure from catastrophic interfacial cracking to ductile void coalescence within the matrix.
The as-cast alloy fractures brittly at strains below 5% because of stress concentration at continuous phase boundaries.
Success requires a thermal window that permits dynamic recovery without excessive grain growth or phase decomposition.
Annealing above the solvus of metastable phases or applying insufficient deformation strain will prevent successful formation of the patterned state.
HIP at up to 200 MPa for two hours provides a pressure-and-temperature-only comparator for the SPD-plus-annealing treatment.

contradictions.description: The rule labels the combination of no HIP improvement and successful SPD-induced improvement as falsification, even though that result would support the claimed SPD-specific effect. Similar improvement after HIP would instead challenge the claimed need for SPD.

The HIP comparator is described as an equivalent-temperature isolation of pressure, but it uses a two-hour exposure whereas the proposed anneal lasts 10–30 minutes. The unequal thermal duration confounds pressure with thermal exposure.
